claims.text: Rain runs down a bus window at night while the city slides past outside.
The glass shows condensation, smudges, irregular droplets, bright rims, and wavering wet trails.
Beyond the pane, blurred streetlights, storefronts, and dark building silhouettes drift through the night.
The city lights remain soft, distant bands and points that swell and shrink with the bus's movement.

description.text: At night, a dark bus-window pane fills the view, its surface scattered with rainwater. Small droplets gather in irregular clusters, each bead catching a tiny, quivering fleck of street light. The beads swell, touch, and merge into heavier drops with bright rims, then begin to slip downward in wavering trails. As they run, the reflections of lights stretch into soft vertical smears and break apart across the wet glass. Faint condensation and smudges give the pane a granular, tactile texture, while the city beyond remains a blurred suggestion of color and shadow. The separate droplets gradually become linked streaks, and every new runnel makes the reflected lights tremble and slide. At the edges of the pane, the reflections are dimmer and more broken, while the central trails carry the brightest color. Each merged bead leaves a fine, wet line that catches the light before fading into the general sheen of the glass. The movement is slow and continuous, drawing the eye down the glass through a quiet, enclosed nocturnal surface.

Beyond the rain-streaked glass, the night city slides steadily past. The wet window still holds the foreground, crossed by long broken trails of water and trembling reflections that overlap the scene outside. Blurred streetlights, lit storefronts, and dark building silhouettes drift across the background, their colors softened by rain and distance. The glass reflections stretch and thin as the city moves, so the near water and the far lights seem to slide against one another. New droplets continue to gather and release, adding fresh streaks while the exterior flows by in a continuous, muted current. The night is deep, and the city never becomes sharp: it remains a sequence of glowing patches and shadowed forms behind the wet pane. The moving lights do not resolve into individual sources; they remain soft bands and pale points that swell and shrink as the bus carries the window onward. The city's motion feels smooth and distant, held behind the close, wet barrier of the glass. The changing balance between the textured glass and the moving lights gives the scene a steady, reflective rhythm, quiet and enclosed even as the outside world travels past.
